summary: MCC-1 Mapping Cleanup Center · backend (12/12 pytest passing) + frontend smoke (all 4 sub-sections, 4 trust tiles, picker dialog) all green. Trust score endpoint returns correct shape with band; driver/asset queues return correct rows; conflicts detection works; former-employee POST bumps resolved count & trust % as expected; admin-strict gating enforced (401/403 without X-Admin-Token); existing autolink regression intact (no signature changes).

issues: Trust tile className concatenates split() array indices which works but is fragile — consider explicit className map for green/amber/red

action_items: Minor: cleanup.py line ~381 weight_resolved math has odd `max(0, max(1,conflict_total)-conflict_total)` pattern that always = 0 when conflicts>0 and 1 when conflicts=0 — confirm intended. Trust formula works in tested data (69.5% with 12 deactivated drivers + 36 unmapped assets) but the conflict_total weighting is non-obvious.
Optional: expose a 'clear cleanup_status' admin endpoint to fully revert a former_employee/ignored mark (current test could not revert state). Not blocking — operator intent is one-way.
Optional: PickerDialog calls /admin/integrations/asset-mappings/unmapped and /employee-mappings/unmapped — confirmed reachable, picker populates with unmapped employees.
critical_code_review_comments: cleanup.py is 735 lines — borderline; consider splitting actions (drivers/assets/conflicts) into separate modules for >700-line rule.
All endpoints properly use _id projection exclusion. Good.
1:1 enforcement on link endpoints correctly returns 409 with explicit message identifying the conflicting mapping_id. Good.
write_sync_log is called on every state mutation — audit trail solid.
Frontend MappingCleanupTab.jsx (700 lines) sits right at the threshold; PickerDialog could be extracted.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing 65 driver / 190 asset mapping data. test_former_employee_bumps_trust_then_revert mutates ONE driver row's cleanup_status to former_employee (data preserved as documented operator intent; no automated revert endpoint exists).
context_for_next_testing_agent: MCC-1 is solid end-to-end. The former-employee test leaves 1 extra driver in resolved state per run — if multiple iterations needed, monitor counts drift in test_trust_score_shape. Conflict resolve was only validation-tested (no live conflicts exist in current preview data per problem statement). To test conflicts live, would need to seed two motive employee_mappings docs pointing at the same masci_employee_id.
